meal.title: Compile C code with gcc
meal.objective: Run gcc to turn C source into an executable binary

voice.script: How does text become a running program? That's what gcc does. gcc is the tool that translates source into a binary. The act of turning source into a binary is called compiling. You open a terminal, type gcc followed by the source file name, and optionally -o and the name you want for the executable. Now we run the compile command. For example, gcc add.c -o add creates a binary called add. If the compiler finds no errors, it finishes silently and you now have an executable you can run. Compiling produces a binary you can execute.
